articles.title: Stable 2-year migration on radiostereometric analysis and improved gait speed and function after bicruciate-retaining TKA: a prospective cohort of 25 patients.
articles.authors: Mills K, Van Laarhoven SN, Defoort KC, Susan S, Heesterbeek PJC
articles.population: Patients undergoing bicruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Component migration measured by radiostereometric analysis at 2 years; gait speed, stride length and stride time measured with wearable sensors; patient-reported outcome measures; adverse events
articles.take_home: The knee implants showed stable fixation at 2 years with minimal movement. Patients reported significant improvements in knee function and quality of life, though walking speed improvements were modest.

articles.title: Arthroplasty versus internal fixation for displaced femoral neck fractures in older patients with dementia: a target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Jensen SS, Gundtoft PH, Nelissen RGHH, Gjertsen JE, Pedersen AB
articles.study_type: Observational comparative-effectiveness study using target trial emulation framework
articles.population: Patients aged 70 years and over with dementia and displaced femoral neck fracture in Denmark
articles.sample_size: 3,161 patients (2,231 receiving arthroplasty, 930 receiving internal fixation)
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: reoperation within 365 days. Secondary outcomes: major reoperation, mortality, length of stay, early mobilisation, and mobility decline
articles.take_home: Internal fixation was associated with fewer reoperations and lower mortality than arthroplasty in older patients with dementia and displaced femoral neck fracture, though the study notes that confounding factors may limit how confidently we can interpret these results as proving one treatment is truly better than the other.

articles.title: Comparative accuracy of large language models and orthopaedic clinicians in knee osteoarthritis and tibial plateau fracture classification systems.
articles.authors: Yigitbay A, Yildirim S
articles.population: 100 radiographic cases from Radiopaedia (20 cases each for five knee and tibial plateau classification systems)
articles.sample_size: 1400 classification assessments from 5 orthopaedic surgeons, 5 residents, and 4 large language models
articles.outcomes: Classification accuracy across Kellgren-Lawrence, Ahlback, Schatzker, Hohl and Moore, and AO/OTA systems
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic surgeons were most accurate at classifying knee and tibial plateau injuries (91.2%), followed by residents (70.2%), whilst large language models were least accurate overall at 51.0%. The AI models performed particularly poorly on Schatzker and Hohl and Moore classifications, suggesting they are not yet reliable for clinical use in orthopaedic diagnosis.

articles.title: Referral Patterns and Clinical Outcomes in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Single-Surgeon Tertiary Care Center Series.
articles.authors: Thota PK, Cohen J, Selemon NA, Sanghavi SA, Sheth NP
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty at a tertiary care centre
articles.outcomes: Hip disability and osteoarthritis outcome scores (HOOS) and re-revision rates at 90 days, one year, two years and final follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients referred from outside the hospital had more previous hip revisions than those referred from within, but both groups achieved similar functional scores after surgery. A history of previous revision surgery was the strongest predictor of needing another revision operation.

articles.title: Porous Tantalum Acetabular Components in Complex Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: The Influence of Defect Severity and Intraoperative Fixation.
articles.authors: D'Apollonio TM, Oteman BPH, Hopman MLT, Abrahams JM, Sheth NP, Solomon LB, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty with porous tantalum acetabular components
articles.outcomes: Acetabular re-revision for aseptic loosening and all-cause acetabular re-revision
articles.take_home: Porous tantalum components performed well in revision hip surgery with very low re-revision rates up to 10 years. The most important factors affecting outcomes were whether the surgeon could achieve a stable three-point fixation and how many previous hip revisions the patient had already had.

articles.title: Custom Triflange Acetabular Components in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: Survivorship, Clinical Outcomes and Risk Factors for Failure.
articles.authors: Kayani B, Drummond I, Merchant AA, Donaldson J, Stammers JG, Sabah SA, et al.
articles.population: Patients with advanced acetabular bone defects undergoing revision hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Component survivorship, Oxford Hip Score, Harris Hip Score, UCLA activity score, WOMAC score, Forgotten Joint Score, radiographic osseointegration, complications, and risk factors for failure
articles.take_home: Custom triflange acetabular components showed good survivorship of 94.3% at mid-term follow-up, with significant improvements in pain and function scores. However, patients who had multiple previous hip operations or extensive bone loss were at higher risk of radiographic failure.

articles.title: Projected Deficiencies in the United States Arthroplasty Workforce: State-Level Shortages of Orthopaedic Surgeons to 2038.
articles.authors: Silvestre J, Leddy LR, Kelly JD, Harris MB, Ahn J, Nelson CL
articles.population: United States orthopaedic surgeon workforce and population demand
articles.outcomes: Projected supply and demand of orthopaedic surgeons by state and region through 2038; geographic disparities in surgeon adequacy
articles.take_home: The study projects that the number of orthopaedic surgeons in the US will not keep pace with demand by 2038, with particularly severe shortages predicted in southern states, non-metropolitan areas, and states like West Virginia and Arkansas. Rural areas face the greatest challenges, with only about half the surgeon capacity needed compared to cities.

articles.title: Physical activity levels two years after total knee arthroplasty and preoperative patient characteristics: a secondary analysis of the MOVE randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Carson NM, Barton KI, Capin JJ, Forster J, Jennings J, Dayton M, et al.
articles.study_type: Secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial
articles.population: Adults aged 50 to 85 years undergoing primary knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Physical activity levels measured by accelerometer at baseline, 10 weeks, 6 months and 2 years after surgery, including light activity, moderate-vigorous activity and steps per day
articles.take_home: Most patients did not return to their pre-surgery activity levels by two years after knee replacement, particularly those who were most active before surgery. The study suggests that current rehabilitation may not fully help patients regain their previous activity levels and additional support might be beneficial.

articles.title: Sepsis Prior to Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Elevated Rates of Myocardial Infarction and Deep Vein Thrombosis.
articles.authors: Alhankawi AR, Holle AM, Renfree SP, Van Schuyver PR, Iturregui-Pastrana JM, Deckey DG, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using insurance database
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective total knee arthroplasty, with and without preoperative sepsis diagnosis
articles.outcomes: 90-day and 2-year postoperative complications including periprosthetic joint infection, sepsis, acute kidney injury, urinary tract infection, blood transfusion, readmission, wound dehiscence, revision surgery, osteomyelitis, myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, and mortality
articles.take_home: Patients who had sepsis in the two years before knee replacement surgery had higher rates of complications within 90 days and at two years, with particularly high risks of heart attack and blood clots if sepsis occurred within three months of surgery.

articles.title: Estimated coronal plane alignment of the knee phenotype transitions after imageless ROSA-assisted total knee arthroplasty are frequent but not significantly associated with short-term patient-reported outcomes.
articles.authors: Kenanidis E, Grammatikopoulos D, Papadopoulos K, Mylonakis N, Maslaris A, Tsiridis E
articles.population: Patients undergoing imageless ROSA-assisted total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Forgotten Joint Score, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index, and Visual Analogue Scale at mean 15.7 months follow-up
articles.take_home: Changes in knee alignment happened in most patients after robotic-assisted knee replacement surgery, but these changes were not linked to worse patient satisfaction or pain scores in the short term. This suggests that preserving the exact pre-surgery alignment may not be necessary for good outcomes.

articles.title: Radiographic patellofemoral differences between end-stage knee rheumatoid arthritis and matched knee osteoarthritis vary by arithmetic hip-knee-ankle-angle-defined coronal alignment.
articles.authors: Liu D, Xie M, Yang S, Chen D, Li H, Weng S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with end-stage knee rheumatoid arthritis or knee osteoarthritis undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 542 matched pairs (669 KRA and 669 KOA knees)
articles.outcomes: Patellofemoral radiographic features including patella baja prevalence, Wiberg type appearance, Insall-Salvati index, lateral patellar displacement, tilt angle, and congruence angle
articles.take_home: Rheumatoid arthritis of the knee shows different patterns of kneecap positioning compared to osteoarthritis, particularly a higher rate of low-sitting kneecaps and outward tilting. These differences were most pronounced in people with knock knees.

articles.title: Wound problems and infections after major joint arthroplasty : national survey results from primary and secondary care in the UK.
articles.authors: Lamb JN, Petheram TG, Lenguerrand E, Whitehouse MR, Moore AJ
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons, microbiologists, general practitioners, physiotherapists, and nursing staff involved in major joint arthroplasty care in the UK
articles.outcomes: Healthcare professionals' views on early wound problems after joint replacement surgery, management strategies, and identification of evidence gaps
articles.take_home: Most healthcare professionals recognise early wound problems after joint replacement are serious and common, but they lack clear guidelines to distinguish superficial from deep infections. There is a strong need for better evidence and clearer guidance to help doctors make the right diagnosis and treatment decisions.

articles.title: Reliability and validity of the My Jump Lab app for assessing vertical jump performance after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Castro DBB, Santana GAM, Carvalho JGB, Bezerra MA, Almeida GPL
articles.population: People 6-24 months after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, cleared for return-to-sport testing
articles.outcomes: Test-retest reliability, validity and agreement of My Jump Lab app compared with force platform for measuring vertical jump performance, jump height, reactive strength index and limb symmetry index
articles.take_home: My Jump Lab is a reliable and valid smartphone app for measuring vertical jump performance after ACL reconstruction, showing excellent consistency and strong agreement with professional force platform equipment. It could be a useful alternative for assessing readiness to return to sport when force platforms are not available.

articles.title: Prediction model-based comparison of medial stabilized and cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty: A two-phase study.
articles.authors: Kimura Y, Takahashi T, Kubo T, Shioiri H, Takeshita K, Matsumoto T
articles.study_type: Retrospective two-phase comparative study with prediction modelling
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement at a single institution
articles.sample_size: 129 cruciate-retaining cases in phase 1; 24 medial stabilised cases in phase 2
articles.outcomes: Postoperative knee flexion (bending) at one year after surgery
articles.take_home: The study found no meaningful difference in knee bending between medial stabilised and cruciate-retaining knee replacements. However, the researchers note that larger studies are needed to draw firm conclusions about which design works better.

articles.title: Tibiofemoral kinematics around heel strike associated with heel strike transient in patients after total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Inou Y, Konda S, Ishibashi T, Tamaki M, Yamazaki T, Okada S, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had undergone total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 17 patients (8 with heel strike transient, 9 without)
articles.outcomes: Tibiofemoral kinematics (knee flexion angle, rotation, anteroposterior translation) and presence of heel strike transient, measured using force plate and 2D/3D registration
articles.take_home: Patients with artificial knees who experience a jarring impact at heel strike show a different knee motion pattern than those without this impact, with their knee extending more abruptly and the contact point shifting forwards on the lateral side of the knee during the transition from swing to stance.

articles.title: Early to mid-term outcomes of the custom-made 3D-printed triflange acetabular component (aMace) : the largest UK dual-centre study.
articles.authors: Khaled AS, Khaliq M, Barrow J, Kwaees TA, Shah N, Wynn Jones H, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision hip arthroplasty for massive acetabular bone loss
articles.sample_size: 52 patients with median follow-up of 51 months
articles.outcomes: No aMace components required revision; reoperation rate 5.7%; leg length discrepancy 9.6%; transient sciatic nerve palsy in 2 cases; significant improvements in pain and mobility (p < 0.001)
articles.take_home: The custom-made 3D-printed aMace component performed well for treating large acetabular bone loss, with none needing revision and low complication rates over 4 years of follow-up. Patients experienced significant improvements in pain and mobility after surgery.

articles.title: Evaluations of the hindfoot before and after total knee arthroplasty for patients with varus and valgus knee osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Iwase D, Metoki Y, Kusumoto Y, Aikawa J, Mukai M, Fukushima K, et al.
articles.population: Patients with varus or valgus knee osteoarthritis undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Hip-knee-ankle angle, mechanical axis percentage, tibial plafond inclination angle, heel alignment distance, knee joint line orientation, mechanical ankle joint axis point, and talar tilt measured on radiographs before surgery and at 6 months
articles.take_home: After knee replacement surgery, the ankle and hindfoot alignment changed differently depending on whether patients had inward or outward bending of the knee before surgery. The study found these radiographic changes but could not confirm whether these changes matter clinically or cause any symptoms.

articles.title: Posterolateral corner deficiency amplifies varus-related anterior cruciate ligament forces under dynamic loading: A biomechanical study.
articles.authors: Gellhaus F, Deichsel A, Stening J, Albert A, Peez C, Behrendt P, et al.
articles.population: Cadaveric knees
articles.outcomes: Anterior cruciate ligament forces under axial loading at various degrees of varus alignment and knee flexion, comparing native knees, posterolateral corner deficiency, and posterolateral corner reconstruction
articles.take_home: When the posterolateral corner of the knee is intact, mild varus (bow-legged) alignment does not significantly increase forces on the anterior cruciate ligament, but severe varus (8 degrees) does. When the posterolateral corner is damaged, even mild varus significantly increases anterior cruciate ligament forces, though reconstruction of the posterolateral corner restores protection.

articles.title: Multicentric development and validation of a fully automated artificial intelligence system for planning medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy on weight-bearing anterior-posterior long leg radiographs: The ISAKOS John Joyce Award 2025.
articles.authors: Rupp MC, von Schacky CE, Lindner FJ, Feucht MJ, Ehmann Y, Fritsch L, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative study with multicentric validation
articles.population: Patients who underwent medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy
articles.sample_size: 594 patients (training and validation); 136 in hold-out testing; 100 in external dataset
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of alignment parameters, reliability (ICC scores), clinically acceptable accuracy rates, and processing time for automated planning versus expert surgeon planning
articles.take_home: An artificial intelligence system can plan knee osteotomy surgery from X-rays as accurately as expert surgeons but much faster (25 seconds versus 2.5 minutes) and with better consistency. This tool could help surgeons plan these operations more reliably and efficiently.

articles.title: Digital tensioning demonstrates smaller medial and larger lateral gap measurements than manual assessment in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Borim FM, Zeng C, Lording T
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty with robotic assistance
articles.outcomes: Comparison of gap measurements between digital tensioning device and manual tensioning with Z-retractor across different knee flexion angles
articles.take_home: Digital tensioning devices showed consistently larger gaps on the outer side of the knee and smaller gaps on the inner side compared to manual measurement techniques. Surgeons using robotic-assisted knee replacement should be aware of these measurement differences when balancing soft tissues during surgery.

articles.title: A mathematical model of knee joint line orientation: Independent effects of femoral and tibial coronal anatomy and limits on achieving a horizontal joint line.
articles.authors: Beckers G, Hengartner M, Lavigne M, Kiss MO, Masse V, Vendittoli PA
articles.population: Representative anthropometric parameters for the lower limb
articles.outcomes: Knee joint line orientation relative to the ground during bipodal and single-limb stance; theoretical mediolateral centre of mass displacement required to achieve horizontal joint line
articles.take_home: The shape of the thigh bone and shin bone independently affect the angle of the knee joint line in ways that can be predicted mathematically. Most people would need to shift their body position significantly to achieve a perfectly horizontal knee joint line, and it is unclear whether this is actually necessary or achievable in practice.

articles.title: Plasma calprotectin as infection biomarker in hip fracture patients: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Pyrhonen HS, Tham J, Stefansdottir A, Persson A, Malmgren L, Rogmark C
articles.population: Hip fracture patients aged 65 years and over treated with surgery
articles.outcomes: Detection of infection within 7 days and 30 days after hip fracture surgery using plasma calprotectin compared with procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, and white blood cell count
articles.take_home: Plasma calprotectin showed modest ability to detect infections after hip fracture surgery, performing slightly better than other blood markers tested, particularly for infections developing within a week. However, all the markers tested only provided moderate diagnostic accuracy overall.
